mechanism_narrative: Because WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain deeply depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, weekday discretionary trips are still suppressed; this should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean for the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES stays below -45 and TRANSIT stays below -50.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL increases further while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain weak, more time at home will substitute away from shopping trips and suppress retail visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 16 while WORKPLACES stays below -50
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 16 and WORKPLACES remains below -50 for at least one week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rebound in PARKS signals broader local mobility normalization and spillover leisure activity, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next month even if workplace travel remains muted.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining above -25 for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls below -60 and WORKPLACES stays below -53 at the same time, access constraints dominate travel behavior and retail trips weaken with a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -60 while WORKPLACES remains below -53
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the next 7 days after both TRANSIT < -60 and WORKPLACES < -53 are observed together.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run improvement in GROCERY_PHARM indicates more routine errand traffic and lower perceived friction for out-of-home trips, which should spill into higher retail-and-recreation mobility within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM posts two consecutive weekly gains.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in PARKS together with a rise in RETAIL_REC over one week implies warm-weather leisure substitution that continues into the following month, keeping retail mobility above its recent average.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -25 and keeps rising
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days after PARKS rises above -25.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, any further easing in transit disruption should transmit quickly into discretionary shopping demand because trip chaining becomes easier and retail visits rise within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after TRANSIT rises above -58.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stop improving while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, the current small gains in discretionary travel will reverse and retail mobility will drift lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES fails to rise above -52 and TRANSIT fails to rise above -57
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining at or below -52 and TRANSIT remaining at or below -57.
